scope: Independent original-fiction English entailment challenge: forty matched premise groups, each with one supported, one contradicted, and one open-world not-established claim. All passages are jointly available evidence; attributed statements establish their occurrence, not their truth unless separately confirmed. No real people or documentary sources are represented. Each group belongs to one of eight phenomena. The set is sealed before frozen argmax predictions and becomes a disclosed regression set after publication, not a future unseen benchmark.

passages.text: The craft register records Theslin as the sole maker of the bowl called Evening Reed. The register lists no date for its creation.
The exhibition record places Evening Reed in the west cabinet throughout opening day. That cabinet and the east cabinet have disjoint interiors, and the bowl is a single physical object.

cases.claim: Theslin made Evening Reed during the year of the exhibition.

citations.quote: The craft register records Theslin as the sole maker of the bowl called Evening Reed. The register lists no date for its creation.
The exhibition record places Evening Reed in the west cabinet throughout opening day. That cabinet and the east cabinet have disjoint interiors, and the bowl is a single physical object.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Neither record supplies a creation year.

passages.text: The posted notice announced that the play would begin at 19:00. In fact, the play began at 19:30 that same evening, as the narrator explicitly confirms. The notice was not changed before the performance.

cases.claim: The notice advertised a start time half an hour earlier than the actual start.

citations.quote: The posted notice announced that the play would begin at 19:00. In fact, the play began at 19:30 that same evening, as the narrator explicitly confirms. The notice was not changed before the performance.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The advertised 19:00 precedes the actual 19:30 by thirty minutes.

passages.text: Mavrik repaired the tower clock without replacing its hands. He replaced the cracked face instead. The account says nothing about work on the clock’s bell.

cases.claim: Mavrik fitted replacement hands to the tower clock.

citations.quote: Mavrik repaired the tower clock without replacing its hands. He replaced the cracked face instead. The account says nothing about work on the clock’s bell.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The premise explicitly states that the hands were not replaced.

passages.text: At noon, the single brass compass was inside a closed drawer in the map room. The map room was inside the western tower. The eastern tower was a separate building with no space in common with the western tower.

cases.claim: At noon, the drawer holding the compass was locked.

citations.quote: At noon, the single brass compass was inside a closed drawer in the map room. The map room was inside the western tower. The eastern tower was a separate building with no space in common with the western tower.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: Closed does not establish locked or unlocked.

passages.text: Olsira finished carving the sign on day 3 of the village fair. She painted it on day 4 and hung it above the gate on day 6. The numbered days belong to the same fair.

cases.claim: Olsira varnished the sign on day 5 of the fair.

citations.quote: Olsira finished carving the sign on day 3 of the village fair. She painted it on day 4 and hung it above the gate on day 6. The numbered days belong to the same fair.

cases.label: not_established
cases.rationale: No varnishing event is given.

passages.text: Exactly six couriers served the island of Velsho. All six carried satchels. Only two of them, Denvik and Alrisa, carried whistles; the other four carried no whistles.

cases.claim: Some satchel-carrying couriers on Velsho carried no whistle.

citations.quote: Exactly six couriers served the island of Velsho. All six carried satchels. Only two of them, Denvik and Alrisa, carried whistles; the other four carried no whistles.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The four without whistles are among the six with satchels.

passages.text: Every apprentice assigned to the north kiln wore gloves during the firing. Senva was one of those apprentices. The passage records no clothing worn by apprentices at the south kiln.

citations.quote: Every apprentice assigned to the north kiln wore gloves during the firing. Senva was one of those apprentices. The passage records no clothing worn by apprentices at the south kiln.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: Senva belongs to the group all of whom wore gloves.

passages.text: At noon, the single brass compass was inside a closed drawer in the map room. The map room was inside the western tower. The eastern tower was a separate building with no space in common with the western tower.

citations.quote: At noon, the single brass compass was inside a closed drawer in the map room. The map room was inside the western tower. The eastern tower was a separate building with no space in common with the western tower.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The compass is in the western tower, and the towers share no space.

passages.text: In this inspection, every crate with a broken seal must be set aside, and that rule was followed without exception. Crate Tavren was not set aside. No other inspection rules or crate properties are stated.

cases.label: contradicted

passages.text: At a gathering in Rethvale, Corvinel said, “The northern well is empty.” This passage establishes only that Corvinel made that statement; it provides no observation or narrator confirmation of the well’s contents.

citations.quote: At a gathering in Rethvale, Corvinel said, “The northern well is empty.” This passage establishes only that Corvinel made that statement; it provides no observation or narrator confirmation of the well’s contents.

cases.label: contradicted
cases.rationale: The premise records the statement denied by the claim.

passages.text: The password gate followed two guaranteed rules during Orlissa’s visit: if the correct word was spoken, its lamp turned green; if its lamp turned green, its latch released. Orlissa spoke the correct word. No rule connected the latch to the door’s movement.

citations.quote: The password gate followed two guaranteed rules during Orlissa’s visit: if the correct word was spoken, its lamp turned green; if its lamp turned green, its latch released. Orlissa spoke the correct word. No rule connected the latch to the door’s movement.

cases.label: supported
cases.rationale: The correct word triggers green, and green triggers latch release.

citations.quote: The warehouse inventory lists exactly eight flour sacks in bin R and exactly seven flour sacks in bin S at 06:00 on Thursday. There were no other flour sacks in those two bins then.
The loading sheet states that every flour sack in bins R and S at 06:00 on Thursday was loaded onto wagon Nelven, and no other sacks were loaded onto that wagon.
